title: Infused virtues real righteousness, yet cannot stand strict divine judgment
source_text: XLIX. Sed quamvis existiment justitiam illam, per quam formaliter coram Deo justificamur, constare fide, spe & charitate, nolunt tamen fidem, & virtutes caeteras constituere justitiam ullam, quae possit ferre rigidum judicii divini examen: ita ut, si Deus fideles districte judicare velit, nec uti erga eos ulla clementia & misericordia, possint per justitiam sibi infusam atque inhaerentem, damnationem vitare, & sperare vitam aeternam. Agnoscunt enim fideles, etiam maxime perfectos, quum se coram severo Dei tribunali sistunt, teneri cum David dicere, Ne intres in judicium cum servo tuo; non enim coram te justificabitur ullus vivens. Idque tum propter peccata, quae justificationem eorum antecedunt: tum propter illa in quae justificati ex infirmitate quotidie labuntur. Itaque mens eorum solum est, virtutes ipsas per Spiritum Sanctum fidelibus infusas, esse formam illam a qua fideles in Scriptura justificati, & justi coram Deo denominantur: & constituere justitiam veram & synceram, non tantum hominum, sed Dei quoque ipsius judicio: quamque Deus quum judex sedebit ultimo die, ex Evangelio mundum judicaturus, solenniter probabit, laudabit, & praemiabitur vita & gloria aeterna.
pass_a_gloss: But although they judge that that righteousness by which we are formally justified before God consists of faith, hope, and charity, they nevertheless do not wish faith and the other virtues to constitute any righteousness that can bear the rigid examination of divine judgment: so that if God should wish to judge the faithful strictly and not use any clemency and mercy toward them, they could not by the righteousness infused and inherent in them avoid damnation and hope for eternal life. For they acknowledge that the faithful, even the most perfect, when they stand before God's severe tribunal, are bound to say with David, Enter not into judgment with your servant; for before you no living person will be justified. And that both because of the sins which precede their justification, and because of those into which the justified daily fall from weakness. Therefore their mind is only that the virtues themselves infused into the faithful by the Holy Spirit are that form by which the faithful are in Scripture denominated justified and just before God; and that they constitute a true and sincere righteousness, not only in men's judgment but also in God's own: which God, when he will sit as judge on the last day to judge the world by the Gospel, will solemnly approve, praise, and reward with eternal life and glory.
pass_b_english: Infused faith-hope-charity is real righteousness in God's sight—yet cannot stand strict judgment without mercy.
Even the perfect must pray Ps 143:2; last-day reward is of gospel promise, not bare legal standing.
